Pilot Sample Size for Minimum Risk Point Estimation of a Mean, Distribution Free

Source: R/seq_mr_dfr_mean_arb.R
seq_mr_dfr_mean_arb_pilot.Rd

Returns the number of observations to collect before the stopping rule of seq_mr_dfr_mean_arb is checked for the first time. That procedure is the purely sequential minimum risk point estimation (MRPE) procedure for the mean of a population whose distribution is not specified and whose variance is unknown and unrestricted (Mukhopadhyay and de Silva, 2009).

Usage

seq_mr_dfr_mean_arb_pilot(A, c, m_0 = 4, gamma = 1)

Arguments

A

The loss constant: the price of one unit of squared estimation error, in the same currency as c, so that the loss is \(A(\bar{X}_n - \mu)^2 + c\,n\). A positive number.

c

The cost of sampling one observation. A positive number.

m_0

The smallest pilot sample size allowed. A whole number of at least 2; default 4.

gamma

The positive constant of the correction term \(n^{-\gamma}\) in the stopping rule; default 1. Use the value passed to seq_mr_dfr_mean_arb.

Value

A length one integer giving the pilot sample size.

Details

The pilot is $$m = \max\{m_0,\ \lceil (A/c)^{1/(2 + 2\gamma)} \rceil\},$$ the pilot sample size of Chattopadhyay and Kelley (2016, Equation 24), who give it for a stopping rule with a correction term of the same kind and present it as following Mukhopadhyay and de Silva (2009). The stopping rule of seq_mr_dfr_mean_arb(), \(n \ge (A/c)^{1/2}(S_n + n^{-\gamma})\), can never be met with fewer than \((A/c)^{1/(2 + 2\gamma)}\) observations, whatever the data, so nothing is lost by collecting that many at the outset. Use the same gamma here and in seq_mr_dfr_mean_arb(). The default values of m_0 and gamma are the package's.

References

Chattopadhyay, B., & Kelley, K. (2016). Estimation of the coefficient of variation with minimum risk: A sequential method for minimizing sampling error and study cost. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 51(5), 627–648. doi:10.1080/00273171.2016.1203279

Mukhopadhyay, N., & de Silva, B. M. (2009). Sequential methods and their applications. Chapman & Hall/CRC. ISBN:9780367386535

See also

seq_mr_dfr_mean_arb

Other seq_mr_dfr_mean_arb: seq_mr_dfr_mean_arb()

Author

Bhargab Chattopadhyay bhargab@iiitvadodara.ac.in, Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# An error of one dollar (squared) in mean order value is worth 400
# dollars to a retailer; auditing one more order costs 0.25 dollars.
seq_mr_dfr_mean_arb_pilot(A = 400, c = 0.25)
#> [1] 7
